title: Implement Soft Delete Pattern with JPA
question: Design a soft delete functionality where records are marked as deleted instead of being physically removed from the database. Requirements: 1) Add 'deleted' boolean flag and 'deletedAt' timestamp to entities, 2) Automatically exclude deleted records from all queries (findAll, findById, etc.), 3) Provide admin-only endpoints to view deleted records, 4) Implement permanent deletion after 90 days retention, 5) Support cascading soft deletes for related entities. Use @Where, @SQLDelete, @Loader annotations or @FilterDef with Hibernate. Discuss: query performance impact with large deleted datasets, index strategy (partial index on non-deleted), cascading soft delete implementation, restoring deleted records, and audit trail considerations.

title: Implement Optimistic Locking to Prevent Lost Updates
question: Your e-commerce system allows multiple admins to edit product inventory simultaneously. Prevent lost updates when two admins edit the same product. Requirements: 1) Use @Version annotation for optimistic locking, 2) Handle OptimisticLockException when concurrent updates occur, 3) Return HTTP 409 Conflict with current data to client, 4) Implement retry mechanism with exponential backoff, 5) Log all conflict occurrences for monitoring. Discuss: optimistic vs pessimistic locking trade-offs, version column type (integer vs timestamp), handling version conflicts in REST API responses, retry strategy (client-side vs server-side), and when optimistic locking is NOT appropriate.

title: Optimize Bulk Insert Performance for Data Migration
question: Migrate 10 million customer records from legacy system to new database. Current approach takes 8 hours. Optimize to complete in under 1 hour. Requirements: 1) Use JDBC batch inserts (batch size 100-1000), 2) Disable second-level cache during import, 3) Clear EntityManager session every N records to avoid memory issues, 4) Choose appropriate ID generation strategy (SEQUENCE performs better than IDENTITY for batch), 5) Disable triggers/constraints temporarily if possible. Achieve 30,000+ inserts per second. Discuss: JDBC batch vs JPA batch performance, optimal batch size calculation, transaction boundary decisions, monitoring progress, handling failures mid-import, and parallel batch processing.

title: Solve N+1 Query Problem in Production Application
question: Your production API endpoint fetches 100 orders with their items and customer details. Currently generating 301 queries (1 for orders + 100 for items + 100 for customers). Response time: 5 seconds. Requirements: 1) Reduce to 1-3 queries using fetch joins or entity graphs, 2) Maintain pagination support, 3) Handle different fetch strategies for different endpoints (list vs details), 4) Monitor and alert on query count per request. Use @EntityGraph, JOIN FETCH in JPQL, or @BatchSize. Discuss: fetch join vs entity graph pros/cons, pagination with fetch joins (MultipleBagFetchException), detecting N+1 in development (hibernate.generate_statistics), query result size impact, and when to denormalize instead.
realWorldScenario: Fixing performance bottleneck from excessive queries

title: Implement Schema-Based Multi-Tenancy with JPA
question: Build a SaaS application serving 1000+ tenants, each with isolated database schema. Single application instance serves all tenants. Requirements: 1) Identify tenant from JWT token or subdomain, 2) Route database queries to correct schema using Hibernate MultiTenantConnectionProvider, 3) Ensure complete data isolation (no cross-tenant data leakage), 4) Support dynamic tenant onboarding without restart, 5) Connection pooling per tenant (HikariCP). Use Hibernate's SCHEMA or DATABASE multi-tenancy strategy. Discuss: tenant context propagation to @Async threads and message consumers, schema migration for all tenants (Flyway), connection pool sizing (1000 tenants = 1000 pools?), handling tenant not found errors, and monitoring per-tenant performance.

title: Optimize Pagination for 50 Million Record Table
question: Customer transaction table has 50 million records. Offset-based pagination (LIMIT 100 OFFSET 1000000) takes 10+ seconds. Requirements: 1) Implement cursor-based (keyset) pagination using indexed columns, 2) Return next/previous cursor tokens, 3) Support sorting by multiple fields, 4) Avoid expensive COUNT query for total pages, 5) Handle deleted records in cursor pagination. Cursor should encode last seen ID + timestamp. Discuss: cursor vs offset pagination trade-offs, cursor encoding/decoding (Base64), handling sort direction changes, ensuring query uses index (EXPLAIN ANALYZE), when offset pagination is acceptable (small datasets, low pages), and cursor limitations (can't jump to arbitrary page).

title: Implement Second-Level Cache with Redis for Read-Heavy Application
question: Product catalog API (read:write ratio 100:1) queries database heavily. Implement second-level cache to reduce database load by 80%. Requirements: 1) Enable Hibernate second-level cache with Redis (hibernate-redis), 2) Cache entities and query results, 3) Invalidate cache on entity updates, 4) Handle cache stampede (thundering herd), 5) Monitor cache hit ratio. Use @Cacheable, @Cache annotations, CacheMode.NORMAL. Discuss: entity cache vs query cache differences, cache eviction strategies (LRU), cache consistency (write-through vs write-behind), handling cache failures (fallback to database), distributed cache coordination across app instances, and warm-up strategy.

title: Implement Read-Write Splitting with Master-Slave Database
question: Scale database reads by routing to read replicas. Setup: 1 master (writes) + 3 read replicas. Requirements: 1) Route write operations to master, reads to replicas, 2) Detect operation type automatically (@Transactional(readOnly=true) for reads), 3) Load balance reads across replicas, 4) Handle replication lag (read-after-write consistency), 5) Remove failed replicas from pool. Use Spring's AbstractRoutingDataSource with custom logic. Discuss: determining read vs write operations reliably, handling replication lag (sticky sessions, version checks), replica health monitoring, failover to master if all replicas down, and connection pool configuration per datasource.

title: Build Complete Audit Trail with Hibernate Envers
question: Regulatory compliance requires tracking all changes to financial transactions. Requirements: 1) Track who changed what and when for all entities, 2) Store complete revision history (not just last modified), 3) Query historical data (get entity state at specific date), 4) Provide audit reports showing change timeline, 5) Handle large audit tables (partitioning). Use Hibernate Envers with @Audited annotation. Discuss: audit table naming (_AUD suffix), revision info customization (username, IP address), performance impact of auditing on writes, audit table storage growth (partitioning by date), querying historical data efficiently, and GDPR compliance (anonymizing audit data).

title: Design Complex Inheritance Hierarchy with JPA
question: Model payment system with base Payment class and subclasses (CreditCardPayment, BankTransferPayment, WalletPayment) each with different fields. Requirements: 1) Choose appropriate inheritance strategy (SINGLE_TABLE, JOINED, or TABLE_PER_CLASS), 2) Support polymorphic queries (find all payments), 3) Optimize for query performance, 4) Handle discriminator column, 5) Consider future addition of new payment types. Discuss: inheritance strategy pros/cons (SINGLE_TABLE vs JOINED), discriminator column (type), query performance implications (joins in JOINED strategy), nullable columns in SINGLE_TABLE, schema migration when adding new subtypes, and when to use composition over inheritance.
